parallel.requirements: Recognized the benchmark as a clean-room XZ Utils 5.8.2 reimplementation with no source lookup, wrapper, or binary analysis shortcuts.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Planned a staged implementation: parent probes and headers, five Wave 1 children for behavior/checks/decoder/encoder/filters, then parent-owned Wave 2 CLI, list, integration, build, and tests.
parallel.implementation: Parent created headers, corpus, compile script, xzfile.c, and check.c; children worked on behavior catalog, lzma decoder, lzma encoder, and filters, leaving a broad set of partial modules.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Final artifact contained partial source files and docs but lacked a complete main program and fully integrated executable implementation path.
parallel.verification: Some module probes and checksum/container compilation checks ran, and a differential harness was written, but no integrated final build/test loop completed before official compile failure.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Wave 1 still had active agents; Wave 2 CLI/main/list/integration/build/differential testing was pending, so the final submission could not compile or satisfy the 2036 official tests.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same XZ 5.8.2 clean-room reimplementation requirements and explored CLI, formats, checks, threading, and encoder behavior from the executable and docs.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Maintained one local todo plan with sequential ownership of probing, checks, LZMA decoder, xz container, encoder, CLI, list mode, filters, and testing.
serial.implementation: Wrote check.h/check.c, lzma_decoder.h/lzma_decoder.c, xzdec.h, and lzma_encoder.h while still reasoning through the LZMA encoder when cancelled.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Delivered only partial source fragments in the artifact, without a complete main program, compile script, integrated encoder/decoder stack, or working executable replacement.
serial.verification: Ran reference probes and some local analysis but did not reach integrated compile, full differential testing, or evaluator-aligned acceptance before cancellation.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The active turn was cancelled during encoder work and the final artifact remained incomplete, producing the same official compile_failed outcome.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run recognized the task as a clean-room XZ Utils 5.8.2 reimplementation requiring behavior learned only from the provided executable and docs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run recognized the same XZ Utils reimplementation obligation and the same prohibitions on source lookup, wrapping, and binary analysis.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference; both understood the breadth of the required executable, including CLI, container, LZMA, checks, filters, and list behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed the work into five detached Wave 1 children and a nested six-child behavior catalog, while reserving Wave 2 CLI, list, integration, build, and tests for later.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept one local task list and proceeded through probing, checks, decoder, container, and encoder work in one actor without delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had much broader concurrent ownership but postponed the end-to-end assembly path; serial had no coordination overhead but also did not finish the same path before cancellation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent created interface headers and detailed briefs before delegation, and the behavior child further subdivided cataloging with its own detailed template.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor carried task knowledge locally through probes and code writes; there were no child briefs, returned handoffs, or cross-agent interfaces to coordinate.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced inter-agent context boundaries but did not show a specific missing requirement or incompatible handoff; serial avoided those boundaries entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced multiple module fragments, including headers, xzfile/check code from the parent, and child-owned decoder/filter work, but no final CLI main or complete encoder implementation in the artifact listing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced checks, decoder headers/source, an xz decoder header, and an encoder header, then stopped while still beginning the core LZMA encoder work.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel covered more modules in breadth; serial progressed linearly into encoder design. Neither delivered a compile-ready complete XZ executable.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had live detached child work, a failed checksum child that the parent took over, and child results/updates continuing after the parent ended its status response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to join; its lifecycle ended by cancellation of the active local turn while implementation was still underway.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's lifecycle risk came from unconsumed and unfinished child waves; serial's closure was a direct incomplete local turn, not a join or takeover problem.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children and parent wrote into the same source tree under nominal file ownership, but closure left only partial modules and no assembled executable source path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote directly into the workspace and its final artifact also contained only partial source files, with no completed assembly path.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more shared-workspace exposure, but the concrete delivered difference was partial breadth versus serial partial depth, not a proven write collision or contamination event.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel performed module-level checks for checksum/container pieces and prepared a differential harness, but never reached whole-executable integrated verification; the official evaluator compile failed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial performed extensive reference probes and some local reasoning, but the run ended before integrated build and acceptance; the official evaluator compile failed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more planned and delegated verification artifacts, while serial had direct exploratory checks, but neither closed the required integrated build/evaluator loop.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used eleven subagents, 345 LLM requests, over 13.5 million tokens, and timed out while Wave 1 was still active and Wave 2 was pending.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, thirty LLM requests, about 1.45 million tokens, and timed out/cancelled during the local encoder work.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both ran out of wall-clock budget, but parallel's distinctive closure problem was excessive fan-out before assembly; serial's was ordinary serial incompletion on a large task.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are concordant failures: both parallel and serial have solution_passed false, error_code compile_failed, and 2036 tests not run. The parallel attempt differed by spending much of the finite run on top-level and nested fan-out before Wave 2 assembly, while the serial attempt failed by remaining an unfinished single-actor implementation.
parallel_contributors: Broad top-level Wave 1 plus nested behavior-catalog fan-out left CLI/main, build integration, and differential testing pending.
Parallel generated more partial module work, but that breadth was not converted into a complete compile-ready deliverable.
serial_contributors: Serial spent the run on one long reverse-engineering and implementation path and was cancelled during core encoder work.
Serial delivered only partial source files and no complete executable implementation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel artifact included files such as filters.c, xzfile.c, lzma_dec.c, and check.c but no complete main.c or lzma_enc.c implementation.
Serial artifact included lzma_encoder.h and decoder/check fragments, but likewise no finished CLI/integration layer.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No outcome difference; retained pattern describes a realized adverse parallel process consequence but not a discordant result cause.

candidates.reason: Implementation owners existed: the parent wrote core modules and assigned LZMA decoder, encoder, checks, filters, and behavior tasks to specific agents; the problem was unfinished breadth, not owner absence.
The parent explicitly reserved the integration stage for Wave 2; integration was not ownerless, it was never reached before budget exhaustion.
The todo list names CLI/main and build assembly as Wave 2 work owned by the parent process, so missing final assembly is a timing/budget consequence rather than absent ownership.
The parent tracked the end-to-end sequence through implementation, integration, build, and differential testing, but the broad first wave consumed the run before that pipeline executed.
No single mandatory preflight blocked all implementation; the parent and several children implemented modules while behavior probing continued.
Investigation was not completed as a separate serial first phase; it overlapped with parent and child implementation work.
The critical CLI/integration path was displaced, but the more specific directly evidenced episode is collective broad fan-out and nested swarm budget exhaustion.

The parallel parent launched five detached Wave 1 agents and one of them launched a six-worker nested swarm; final parent-visible state still had Wave 1 active and Wave 2 assembly, build, and differential testing pending.
candidates.realized_consequence: The broad top-level and nested first-wave fan-out consumed the finite run before CLI/main assembly, full build integration, and differential testing could start.
candidates.near_match_reason: A critical path was left pending, but the specific observed boundary is excessive collective breadth across top-level and nested children, not a narrower underallocation episode.

No known requirement or finding is shown disappearing through transfer and causing repeated work; the main failure was that results were not reached in time.
The behavior-catalog result was bulky, but there is no parent decision window where the parent received it and failed to reduce it; the parent had already closed.
No receiver acted on superseded workspace or requirement information; stale todo reminders were noticed and not used as authoritative state.
No incompatible child reports or contracts reached the parent and remained unadjudicated at a decision point.
The parent did not present the whole task as complete; it explicitly reported only partial completed modules and pending Wave 2 work.
There was no replacement or retry episode that restarted without inherited findings or current workspace state.

There was no integrated verification that preceded a later merge; the run never reached integrated verification.
Completed delegated implementation that reached the workspace was already present as source fragments, and no complete retrievable implementation was ignored in favor of a worse final build.

The checksum child failed, and the parent explicitly took that module over by writing check.c itself; other unfinished children were not failed scopes with a distinct no-takeover episode.
No parent-visible completed implementation result is shown being ignored; behavior catalog output arrived after the parent had already ended.
The parent inspected progress and updated todo state; the terminal problem was broad fan-out exhausting budget, not passive waiting without inspection.
Agents wrote different modules, but their scopes were intentionally separated by headers and file ownership; no competing designs required reconciliation.
The only same-file rewrite was parent takeover of check.c after the child failure, not two live agents editing and reconciling the same file concurrently.
Parent rewriting check.c after a failed child did not produce an adverse overwrite consequence; it was an explicit takeover of a small module.
No required executable or entry-point source was overwritten while another agent owned or used it; no main.c or final executable was delivered.
There was no broad cleanup or promotion that replaced another actor's final-tree work.
The workspace was shared, but no concrete unstable-state or provenance problem beyond unfinished breadth is evidenced.
Scratch files and stale todo reminders were visible, but no generated artifact or cache from one actor was consumed as stable input in a way that contaminated the delivered tree.
